তারিখ: ১৮ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪২৯ বঙ্গাব্দ/ ১ জুন, ২০২২ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

এস,আর,ও নং ১৪৮-আইন/২০২২/৯৬/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 19 এর sub-section (1) এবং মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক আইন, ২০১২ (২০১২ সনের ৪৭ নং আইন) এর ধারা ১২৬ এর উপ-ধারা (১) এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, ২৪ মে, ২০২১ খ্রিস্টাব্দ মোতাবেক ১০ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪২৮ তারিখে জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপন এস,আর,ও নং ১২০-আইন/২০২১/০৯/কাস্টমস এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act provides the government with the authority to issue notifications, including those that amend or rescind previous customs orders, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act provides the legal basis and authority for the government to issue notifications related to customs and taxation adjustments.
National Board of Revenue: The government is mandated to consult with this body when exercising its legal authority to issue or amend customs notifications.
S.R.O. 120-AIN/2021: This existing customs notification, originally issued in May 2021, is subject to further amendment by the current order.

TABLE-2: This table lists specific raw materials or inputs whose annual import volume must be estimated based on production capacity and annual planning.
TABLE-3: This table provides the categories or specific items for which annual import projections must be submitted to customs and VAT authorities.
Customs Authority: Importers are required to submit an annual consumption and production estimate to the relevant Customs House or Customs Station commissioner every January.
The Commissioner of the relevant Customs House or Customs Station is responsible for clearing imported goods based on the approved annual estimates.
Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate: This body is responsible for conducting physical audits every six months to ensure that imported materials are actually being used for the declared manufacturing purposes.
Upon completion of an audit, the Commissioner must submit an objective report within one month to the National Board of Revenue and share a copy with the relevant customs authorities.

In cases where the misuse of duty-concessionary imports is discovered, this commissioner is authorized to request the relevant Customs Commissioner to initiate legal action under the specific offence provisions of the Customs Act.
National Board of Revenue: The Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate must submit an audit report on the utilization of imported inputs to the Member (Customs: Policy) of the National Board of Revenue.
Customs Act 1969: If an audit reveals the misuse of inputs imported at concessional rates, legal actions are to be taken in accordance with the provisions specified in the Table of Section 156 of the Customs Act.

৪। কাস্টমস, এক্সাইজ ও ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট কর্তৃক নিরীক্ষায় প্রাপ্ত ফলাফল :
৫। ক্রমিক নং-৩ ও ৪ এর পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে কমিশনারেটের পর্যবেক্ষণ/ সুপারিশ/ পদক্ষেপ :

                                      -------------------।”।

TABLE: The table serves as a reference for reporting imported materials during the audit period.
The table is used to list specific imported raw materials on a bill of entry basis for the purpose of customs audit compliance.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is the designated authority responsible for conducting audits and documenting findings related to imported materials.
The Commissioner is tasked with providing observations, recommendations, or taking necessary actions based on the outcomes of the audit conducted by the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate.
Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate: This body is responsible for performing audits of imported materials for a specified period.
The Commissionerate oversees the reporting process and records its findings, recommendations, and subsequent actions regarding import compliance.
